From 25236c91b5ab4a26a56ba2e79b8060cf4e047839 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Feb 2024 14:04:53 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] af_unix: Fix task hung while purging oob_skb in GC.

syzbot reported a task hung; at the same time, GC was looping infinitely
in list_for_each_entry_safe() for OOB skb.  [0]

syzbot demonstrated that the list_for_each_entry_safe() was not actually
safe in this case.

A single skb could have references for multiple sockets.  If we free such
a skb in the list_for_each_entry_safe(), the current and next sockets could
be unlinked in a single iteration.

unix_notinflight() uses list_del_init() to unlink the socket, so the
prefetched next socket forms a loop itself and list_for_each_entry_safe()
never stops.

Here, we must use while() and make sure we always fetch the first socket.

Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=4fa4a2d1f5a5ee06f006
Fixes: 1279f9d9dec2 ("af_unix: Call kfree_skb() for dead unix_(sk)->oob_skb in GC.")
Signed-off-by: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@amazon.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240209220453.96053-1-kuniyu@amazon.com

diff --git a/net/unix/garbage.c b/net/unix/garbage.c
index 8f63f0b4bf01..2ff7ddbaa782 100644
--- a/net/unix/garbage.c
+++ b/net/unix/garbage.c
@@ -315,10 +315,11 @@ void unix_gc(void)
 	__skb_queue_purge(&hitlist);
 
 #if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_AF_UNIX_OOB)
-	list_for_each_entry_safe(u, next, &gc_candidates, link) {
-		struct sk_buff *skb = u->oob_skb;
+	while (!list_empty(&gc_candidates)) {
+		u = list_entry(gc_candidates.next, struct unix_sock, link);
+		if (u->oob_skb) {
+			struct sk_buff *skb = u->oob_skb;
 
-		if (skb) {
 			u->oob_skb = NULL;
 			kfree_skb(skb);
 		}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/unix/garbage.c`**
   - The loop that processes the garbage collection candidates has been changed from `list_for_each_entry_safe()` to a `while` loop that checks if the `gc_candidates` list is not empty.
   - The first socket in the list is fetched using `list_entry(gc_candidates.next, struct unix_sock, link)` instead of relying on the safe iteration method.
   - The `oob_skb` of the socket is set to `NULL` after it is freed, ensuring that the socket is properly unlinked.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `net/unix/garbage.c` address a bug where the original use of `list_for_each_entry_safe()` could lead to an infinite loop when freeing sockets that had multiple references. By switching to a `while` loop and explicitly fetching the first socket, the patch ensures that the garbage collection process can safely unlink and free the `oob_skb` without causing a loop in the list. This change directly resolves the issue reported by syzbot regarding task hangs during garbage collection.
